claim: Psychosis is characterized by a diminished ability of the brain to distinguish externally driven activity patterns from self-generated activity patterns.
source: Psychosis is characterized by a diminished ability of the brain to distinguish externally driven activity patterns from self-generated activity patterns.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that draws from established understanding of psychosis in the scientific literature.

claim: Antipsychotic drugs are a class of small molecules with relatively broad binding affinity for a variety of neuromodulator receptors.
source: Antipsychotic drugs are a class of small molecules with relatively broad binding affinity for a variety of neuromodulator receptors that, in humans, can prevent or ameliorate psychosis.
evidence: This is a statement about the pharmacological properties of antipsychotic drugs, which is established knowledge in pharmacology.

claim: Antipsychotic drugs can prevent or ameliorate psychosis in humans.
source: Antipsychotic drugs are a class of small molecules with relatively broad binding affinity for a variety of neuromodulator receptors that, in humans, can prevent or ameliorate psychosis.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical efficacy of antipsychotic drugs, which is established knowledge in psychiatry.

claim: Deep cortical layers were differentially activated during locomotion onsets that were experimentally coupled to self-generated visual feedback compared to locomotion onsets that were not coupled.
source: By comparing cell type-specific activation patterns between locomotion onsets that were experimentally coupled to self-generated visual feedback and locomotion onsets that were not coupled, we show that deep cortical layers were differentially activated in these two conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing closed loop and open loop conditions shown in the figures.

claim: The antipsychotic drug clozapine disrupted visuomotor integration at locomotion onsets primarily in deep cortical layers.
source: We then show that the antipsychotic drug clozapine disrupted visuomotor integration at locomotion onsets also primarily in deep cortical layers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the effects of clozapine on locomotion onset responses in deep cortical layers.

claim: Clozapine resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas.
source: We found that clozapine as well as two other antipsychotic drugs, aripiprazole and haloperidol, resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas and impaired the spread of visuomotor prediction errors generated in visual cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing correlation analyses before and after drug administration.

claim: Aripiprazole resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas.
source: We found that clozapine as well as two other antipsychotic drugs, aripiprazole and haloperidol, resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas and impaired the spread of visuomotor prediction errors generated in visual cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing correlation analyses before and after drug administration.

claim: Haloperidol resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas.
source: We found that clozapine as well as two other antipsychotic drugs, aripiprazole and haloperidol, resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas and impaired the spread of visuomotor prediction errors generated in visual cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing correlation analyses before and after drug administration.

claim: Antipsychotic drugs impaired the spread of visuomotor prediction errors generated in visual cortex.
source: We found that clozapine as well as two other antipsychotic drugs, aripiprazole and haloperidol, resulted in a strong reduction in correlations of layer 5 activity between cortical areas and impaired the spread of visuomotor prediction errors generated in visual cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced spread of prediction error responses after drug administration.

claim: A major functional effect of antipsychotic drugs is a selective alteration of long-range layer 5-mediated communication.
source: Our results are consistent with the interpretation that a major functional effect of antipsychotic drugs is a selective alteration of long-range layer 5-mediated communication.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results showing selective effects on layer 5 correlations and prediction error spread.

claim: Self-generated movements are coupled to sensory feedback in different modalities under normal conditions.
source: Under normal conditions, self-generated movements are coupled to sensory feedback in different modalities.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about sensorimotor integration.

claim: Locomotion is coupled to proprioceptive feedback from muscle movements.
source: Locomotion, for example, is coupled to proprioceptive feedback from muscle movements, somatosensory and auditory feedback from touching the ground, vestibular feedback from translational acceleration, and visual feedback in the form of expanding visual flow.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about sensorimotor integration during locomotion.

claim: Locomotion is coupled to somatosensory and auditory feedback from touching the ground.
source: Locomotion, for example, is coupled to proprioceptive feedback from muscle movements, somatosensory and auditory feedback from touching the ground, vestibular feedback from translational acceleration, and visual feedback in the form of expanding visual flow.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about sensorimotor integration during locomotion.

claim: Locomotion is coupled to vestibular feedback from translational acceleration.
source: Locomotion, for example, is coupled to proprioceptive feedback from muscle movements, somatosensory and auditory feedback from touching the ground, vestibular feedback from translational acceleration, and visual feedback in the form of expanding visual flow.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about sensorimotor integration during locomotion.

claim: Locomotion is coupled to visual feedback in the form of expanding visual flow.
source: Locomotion, for example, is coupled to proprioceptive feedback from muscle movements, somatosensory and auditory feedback from touching the ground, vestibular feedback from translational acceleration, and visual feedback in the form of expanding visual flow.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about sensorimotor integration during locomotion.

claim: The coupling between movement and sensory feedback is key to the brain's ability to learn internal models of the world.
source: This coupling is key to our brain's ability to learn internal models of the world (Jordan and Rumelhart, 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jordan and Rumelhart, 1992.

claim: Internal models are the transformations between cortical areas and can be used to predict the sensory consequences of movement.
source: Internal models are the transformations between cortical areas and can be used to predict the sensory consequences of movement.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about internal models in neuroscience.

claim: Hallucinations and delusions can be explained as a misconfiguration of internal models.
source: Hallucinations and delusions can be explained as a misconfiguration of these internal models: inaccurate predictions of the sensory consequences of movements can result in self-generated activity that is not correctly distinguished from externally driven activity (Fletcher and Frith, 2009; Frith, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fletcher and Frith, 2009 and Frith, 2005.

claim: Inaccurate predictions of the sensory consequences of movements can result in self-generated activity that is not correctly distinguished from externally driven activity.
source: Hallucinations and delusions can be explained as a misconfiguration of these internal models: inaccurate predictions of the sensory consequences of movements can result in self-generated activity that is not correctly distinguished from externally driven activity (Fletcher and Frith, 2009; Frith, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fletcher and Frith, 2009 and Frith, 2005.

claim: Self-generated movements result in broad activation of most regions of the brain.
source: Self-generated movements result in broad activation of most regions of the brain (Musall et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019), including some primary sensory areas like visual cortex (Keller et al., 2012; Saleem et al., 2013) where they have been shown to depend on visual context (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Musall et al., 2019 and Stringer et al., 2019.

claim: Self-generated movements result in activation of primary sensory areas like visual cortex.
source: Self-generated movements result in broad activation of most regions of the brain (Musall et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019), including some primary sensory areas like visual cortex (Keller et al., 2012; Saleem et al., 2013) where they have been shown to depend on visual context (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Keller et al., 2012 and Saleem et al., 2013.

claim: Movement-related signals in visual cortex depend on visual context.
source: Self-generated movements result in broad activation of most regions of the brain (Musall et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019), including some primary sensory areas like visual cortex (Keller et al., 2012; Saleem et al., 2013) where they have been shown to depend on visual context (Pakan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pakan et al., 2016.

claim: The framework of predictive processing postulates that movement-related signals in cortex are internal model-based predictions of the sensory consequences of movement that are compared to externally generated bottom-up input to compute prediction errors.
source: The framework of predictive processing postulates that in cortex, these movement-related signals are internal model-based predictions of the sensory consequences of movement that are compared to externally generated bottom-up input to compute prediction errors (Jiang and Rao, 2021; Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jiang and Rao, 2021 and Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018.

claim: Movement-related prediction error responses have been discovered in a variety of different cortical regions and species.
source: Evidence for this interpretation has mainly come from the discovery of movement-related prediction error responses in a variety of different cortical regions and species (Attinger et al., 2017; Audette et al., 2021; Ayaz et al., 2019; Eliades and Wang, 2008; Heindorf et al., 2018; Keller et al., 2012; Keller and Hahnloser, 2009; Stanley and Miall, 2007; Zmarz and Keller, 2016), and the observation that top-down inputs from motor areas of cortex appear to convey movement-related predictions of sensory input to sensory areas of cortex (Leinweber et al., 2017; Schneider et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies showing prediction error responses.

claim: Top-down inputs from motor areas of cortex appear to convey movement-related predictions of sensory input to sensory areas of cortex.
source: Evidence for this interpretation has mainly come from the discovery of movement-related prediction error responses in a variety of different cortical regions and species (Attinger et al., 2017; Audette et al., 2021; Ayaz et al., 2019; Eliades and Wang, 2008; Heindorf et al., 2018; Keller et al., 2012; Keller and Hahnloser, 2009; Stanley and Miall, 2007; Zmarz and Keller, 2016), and the observation that top-down inputs from motor areas of cortex appear to convey movement-related predictions of sensory input to sensory areas of cortex (Leinweber et al., 2017; Schneider et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Leinweber et al., 2017 and Schneider et al., 2018.

claim: Prediction error neurons are thought to reside primarily in layer 2/3 of cortex.
source: The neurons on which the opposing bottom-up input and top-down prediction converge are referred to as prediction error neurons and are thought to reside primarily in layer 2/3 (L2/3) of cortex (Jordan and Keller, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jordan and Keller, 2020.

claim: It has been speculated that internal representation neurons can be found in deep cortical layers based on anatomical arguments.
source: It is still unclear which cortical neuron type functions as internal representation neurons, but based on anatomical arguments it has been speculated that they can be found in deep cortical layers (Bastos et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bastos et al., 2012 and is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: Locomotion onset in the closed loop condition resulted in broad activation across most of dorsal cortex in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide.
source: Consistent with previous findings (Musall et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019), we found that locomotion onset resulted in broad activation across most of dorsal cortex in both conditions (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and is consistent with cited previous findings.

claim: Locomotion onset in the open loop condition resulted in broad activation across most of dorsal cortex in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide.
source: Consistent with previous findings (Musall et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019), we found that locomotion onset resulted in broad activation across most of dorsal cortex in both conditions (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and is consistent with cited previous findings.

claim: In Tlx3 positive layer 5 IT neurons, locomotion onset in the open loop condition resulted in an increase in activity across dorsal cortex.
source: While locomotion onset in the open loop condition resulted in an increase in activity across dorsal cortex, similar to that observed in C57BL/6 mice with brain wide GCaMP expression, locomotion onset in the closed loop condition resulted in a very different activation pattern: In posterior parts of dorsal cortex, the activity decreased, while in anterior parts of the dorsal cortex, the activity increased.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing closed and open loop conditions in Tlx3 mice.

claim: In Tlx3 positive layer 5 IT neurons, locomotion onset in the closed loop condition resulted in decreased activity in posterior parts of dorsal cortex and increased activity in anterior parts of dorsal cortex.
source: While locomotion onset in the open loop condition resulted in an increase in activity across dorsal cortex, similar to that observed in C57BL/6 mice with brain wide GCaMP expression, locomotion onset in the closed loop condition resulted in a very different activation pattern: In posterior parts of dorsal cortex, the activity decreased, while in anterior parts of the dorsal cortex, the activity increased.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing closed and open loop conditions in Tlx3 mice.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, visual flow onsets resulted in responses that were small compared to those observed during locomotion onset, even in V1.
source: In C57BL/6 mice with brain wide GCaMP expression, visual flow onsets resulted in responses that were small compared to those observed during locomotion onset, even in V1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing visual flow onset and locomotion onset responses.

claim: A visual flow onset is a relatively weak visual stimulus compared to a drifting grating stimulus.
source: Note that a visual flow onset is a relatively weak visual stimulus compared to a drifting grating stimulus.
evidence: This is a statement based on the experimental design and the nature of the stimuli used.

claim: A grating stimulus is typically composed of a gray screen or a standing grating stimulus that suddenly transitions to a drifting grating, and thus the visual flow undergoes a very high acceleration.
source: A grating stimulus is typically composed of a gray screen or a standing grating stimulus that suddenly transitions to a drifting grating, and thus the visual flow undergoes a very high acceleration.
evidence: This is a statement based on the experimental design and the nature of the stimuli used.

claim: A visual flow onset in an open loop condition is the replay of previously self-generated visual flow and thus exhibits much lower visual flow acceleration.
source: A visual flow onset in an open loop condition is the replay of previously self-generated visual flow and thus exhibits much lower visual flow acceleration.
evidence: This is a statement based on the experimental design and the nature of the stimuli used.

claim: The absence of a strong visual flow onset response in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide is consistent with a high similarity of closed and open loop locomotion onset responses.
source: The absence of a strong visual flow onset response in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide is consistent with a high similarity of closed and open loop locomotion onset responses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing visual flow onset and locomotion onset responses.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the closed loop locomotion onset patterns differed markedly when compared across the six ROIs.
source: Different from what we found in mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, in mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the closed loop locomotion onset patterns differed markedly when compared across the six ROIs (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, closed loop locomotion onset activation patterns were different from those observed during open loop locomotion onsets.
source: Moreover, these activation patterns were different from those observed during open loop locomotion onsets (Figure 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The time course of hemodynamic occlusion in Tlx3-Cre mice that expressed eGFP in L5 IT neurons was similar to that observed in C57BL/6 mice that expressed eGFP brain wide and mainly resulted in a decrease of fluorescence.
source: While these responses could partially be explained by hemodynamic occlusion, the time course of hemodynamic occlusion in Tlx3-Cre mice that expressed eGFP in L5 IT neurons was similar to that observed in C57BL/6 mice that expressed eGFP brain wide and mainly resulted in a decrease of fluorescence (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: In Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, open loop visual flow onsets that occurred in the absence of locomotion resulted in quantifiable responses in V1 and V2am.
source: In Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, open loop visual flow onsets that occurred in the absence of locomotion resulted in quantifiable responses in V1 and V2am (Figure 1K), but the closed loop locomotion onset responses in V1 could not be explained by the sum of locomotion and visual flow onset responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: The closed loop locomotion onset responses in V1 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons could not be explained by the sum of locomotion and visual flow onset responses.
source: In Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, open loop visual flow onsets that occurred in the absence of locomotion resulted in quantifiable responses in V1 and V2am (Figure 1K), but the closed loop locomotion onset responses in V1 could not be explained by the sum of locomotion and visual flow onset responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and C.

claim: Most of the widefield signals recorded likely originate in compartments in superficial layers which are composed of axons and dendrites of local neurons, and long-range inputs.
source: Most of the widefield signals we record here likely originate in compartments in superficial layers which are composed of axons and dendrites of local neurons, and long-range inputs (Allen et al., 2017) (see Discussion).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Allen et al., 2017.

claim: There were differences between the responses measured with widefield imaging and those measured at the soma in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, both for locomotion onset responses and for visual responses.
source: We found that while there were differences between the responses measured with widefield imaging and those measured at the soma, both for locomotion onset responses and for visual responses, these differences did not change our conclusions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The differences between widefield and somatic responses in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons did not change the conclusions.
source: We found that while there were differences between the responses measured with widefield imaging and those measured at the soma, both for locomotion onset responses and for visual responses, these differences did not change our conclusions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of widefield and two-photon imaging data.

claim: The similarity in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons was lower than that observed in all other neuron types tested, except for Ntsr1 positive L6 neurons.
source: Quantifying the differences in V1, we find that the similarity in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons was lower than that observed in all other neuron types tested, except for Ntsr1 positive L6 neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 4J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4J.

claim: C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide exhibited the highest similarity between closed and open loop locomotion onsets across regions.
source: Both in V1 across mice, as well as when comparing across all areas, we found the highest similarity between closed and open loop locomotion onsets across regions in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing similarity across different neuron types.

claim: Among the neuron types tested, excitatory neurons of deep cortical layers exhibited the largest differences between closed and open loop locomotion-related activation across all the selected cortical regions.
source: Thus, among the neuron types tested, excitatory neurons of deep cortical layers exhibited the largest differences between closed and open loop locomotion-related activation across all the selected cortical regions.
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the experimental data comparing different neuron types.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, the correlation between calcium activity and locomotion speed was comparable between closed and open loop conditions.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, this correlation was comparable between closed and open loop conditions, was highest in posterior regions of dorsal cortex, and lower in more anterior regions (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, the correlation between calcium activity and locomotion speed was highest in posterior regions of dorsal cortex and lower in more anterior regions.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, this correlation was comparable between closed and open loop conditions, was highest in posterior regions of dorsal cortex, and lower in more anterior regions (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in the closed loop condition was negative in posterior regions of dorsal cortex and positive in anterior regions.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in the closed loop condition was negative in posterior regions of dorsal cortex and positive in anterior regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing correlations in different cortical regions.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in open loop conditions was positive throughout dorsal cortex.
source: Conversely, in open loop conditions, the correlation was positive throughout dorsal cortex (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, the correlation of calcium activity with locomotion in darkness was indistinguishable from that in closed or open loop.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, the correlation of calcium activity with locomotion in darkness was indistinguishable from that in closed or open loop (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in relative darkness in visual regions resembled that observed in open loop conditions.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, an interesting pattern emerged. In visual regions of dorsal cortex, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in relative darkness resembled that observed in open loop conditions, while in frontal regions, it resembled that observed in closed loop conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing correlations in different conditions.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in relative darkness in frontal regions resembled that observed in closed loop conditions.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, an interesting pattern emerged. In visual regions of dorsal cortex, the correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in relative darkness resembled that observed in open loop conditions, while in frontal regions, it resembled that observed in closed loop conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing correlations in different conditions.

claim: In visual regions, the coupling of visual flow resulted in a reduction of correlation between locomotion speed and calcium activity in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: In visual regions, the coupling of visual flow resulted in a reduction of correlation, while in frontal regions the presence of an uncoupled visual stimulus resulted in an increase of correlations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing correlations in different conditions.

claim: In frontal regions, the presence of an uncoupled visual stimulus resulted in an increase of correlations between locomotion speed and calcium activity in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: In visual regions, the coupling of visual flow resulted in a reduction of correlation, while in frontal regions the presence of an uncoupled visual stimulus resulted in an increase of correlations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing correlations in different conditions.

claim: The difference between closed and open loop conditions likely had different origins in visual and frontal regions of dorsal cortex.
source: Thus, the difference between closed and open loop conditions likely had different origins in visual and frontal regions of dorsal cortex.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing correlations in different regions and conditions.

claim: The coupling of locomotion and resulting visual flow feedback activated Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons differentially throughout dorsal cortex, well beyond visual regions.
source: Overall, we concluded that the coupling of locomotion and resulting visual flow feedback not only activated Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons differentially but did so throughout dorsal cortex, well beyond visual regions.
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the experimental data showing differential activation across cortical regions.

claim: Predictions are used to compute prediction errors in L2/3 of cortex.
source: It has been speculated that such predictions are used to compute prediction errors in L2/3 of cortex (Jordan and Keller, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jordan and Keller, 2020 and is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: Prediction errors come in two variants: Positive prediction errors that signal more visual flow than predicted and negative prediction errors that signal less visual flow than predicted.
source: Prediction errors come in two variants: Positive prediction errors that signal more visual flow than predicted and negative prediction errors that signal less visual flow than predicted (Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018; Rao and Ballard, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018 and Rao and Ballard, 1999.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, both visuomotor mismatch and grating stimuli resulted in increases of activity that were strongest and appeared first in visual regions of dorsal cortex.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, both visuomotor mismatch and grating stimuli resulted in increases of activity that were strongest and appeared first in visual regions of dorsal cortex (Figure 3A–C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A–C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, visuomotor mismatch resulted in an increase of activity in V1.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, visuomotor mismatch resulted in an increase of activity in V1, while grating onsets resulted in a decrease of activity in V1 (Figure 3D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, grating onsets resulted in a decrease of activity in V1.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, visuomotor mismatch resulted in an increase of activity in V1, while grating onsets resulted in a decrease of activity in V1 (Figure 3D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D–F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: In dorsal cortex, both mismatch and drifting grating stimuli primarily activated visual cortex but resulted in opposing activation patterns in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: Thus, in dorsal cortex, both mismatch and drifting grating stimuli primarily activated visual cortex but resulted in opposing activation patterns in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the experimental data showing opposing responses to different stimuli.

claim: An increase in activity to negative prediction errors and a decrease to positive prediction errors would be consistent with either a population of negative prediction error neurons or a type of internal representation neuron.
source: An increase in activity to negative prediction errors and a decrease to positive prediction errors would be consistent with either a population of negative prediction error neurons or a type of internal representation neuron (Rao and Ballard, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rao and Ballard, 1999 and represents an interpretation of the data.

claim: L5 neurons in V1 do not exhibit the opposing influence of top-down and bottom-up inputs necessary to compute prediction errors.
source: Given that L5 neurons in V1 do not exhibit the opposing influence of top-down and bottom-up inputs necessary to compute prediction errors (Jordan and Keller, 2020), we speculated that Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons might function as a type of internal representation neuron.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jordan and Keller, 2020.

claim: Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons might function as a type of internal representation neuron.
source: Given that L5 neurons in V1 do not exhibit the opposing influence of top-down and bottom-up inputs necessary to compute prediction errors (Jordan and Keller, 2020), we speculated that Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons might function as a type of internal representation neuron.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation based on the experimental data and cited literature.

claim: The activation of an internal representation is the brain's best guess at what the stimuli in the environment are.
source: The activation of an internal representation is the brain's best guess at what the stimuli in the environment are.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about internal representations in neuroscience.

claim: The activation of an internal representation would be particularly susceptible to substances that are known to reduce illusory percepts, like antipsychotic drugs.
source: We speculated that the activation of such an internal representation would be particularly susceptible to substances that are known to reduce illusory percepts, like antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, closed and open loop locomotion onsets were almost unaffected by clozapine.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, we found that closed and open loop locomotion onsets were almost unaffected by clozapine (Figure 4A and B), while there was a small increase in open loop visual flow onset responses (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, there was a small increase in open loop visual flow onset responses after clozapine administration.
source: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, we found that closed and open loop locomotion onsets were almost unaffected by clozapine (Figure 4A and B), while there was a small increase in open loop visual flow onset responses (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, clozapine fundamentally changed both closed and open loop locomotion onset responses.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, however, clozapine fundamentally changed both closed and open loop locomotion onset responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing responses before and after clozapine administration.

claim: In V1 of mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, both closed and open loop locomotion onsets resulted in a massive increase in activity after clozapine administration.
source: In V1, both types of locomotion onset now resulted in a massive increase in activity (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, open loop visual flow onset responses remained largely unchanged after clozapine administration.
source: Conversely, open loop visual flow onset responses remained largely unchanged (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The effects of clozapine on locomotion onset responses in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons could not be explained by clozapine-induced changes in hemodynamic occlusion.
source: These effects could not be explained by clozapine-induced changes in hemodynamic occlusion (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) or locomotion behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The effects of clozapine on locomotion onset responses in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons could not be explained by clozapine-induced changes in locomotion behavior.
source: These effects could not be explained by clozapine-induced changes in hemodynamic occlusion (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) or locomotion behavior (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Clozapine had an opposing effect on the average correlation of activity with locomotion speed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons compared to C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide.
source: Clozapine also had an opposing effect on the average correlation of activity with locomotion speed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons. While the average correlation between activity and locomotion speed was increased in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, the same measure was decreased in mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: After clozapine administration, an increase of somatic responses during locomotion onsets was observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons using two-photon imaging that was very similar to that observed with widefield imaging.
source: Finally, we confirmed that this effect was also present when recording somatic activity in V1. Using two-photon imaging, after clozapine administration we observed an increase of somatic responses during locomotion onsets that was very similar to that observed with widefield imaging (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Clozapine exhibited a substantially stronger influence on locomotion onset responses in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons than would be expected from the effect of clozapine on brain wide responses.
source: Thus, consistent with the speculation that Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons might function as internal representation neurons, clozapine exhibited a substantially stronger influence on locomotion onset responses in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons than would be expected from the effect of clozapine on brain wide responses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing the effects of clozapine in different neuron types.

claim: L5 IT neurons are likely the primary source of long-range cortical communication.
source: L5 IT neurons are likely the primary source of long-range cortical communication (Chen et al., 2019; Harris et al., 2019; Leinweber et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2019, Harris et al., 2019, and Leinweber et al., 2017.

claim: Clozapine resulted in a relatively modest decrease in correlations of calcium activity between ROIs in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide.
source: Overall, clozapine resulted in a relatively modest decrease in correlations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing correlations before and after clozapine administration.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, clozapine resulted in a larger decrease in correlations that appeared to be stronger for regions that were further apart.
source: On repeating this experiment in mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, we found a larger decrease in correlations that appeared to be stronger for regions that were further apart (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, both short- and long-range correlations were reduced by clozapine, but this reduction was not significant in either case.
source: While both short- and long-range correlations were reduced, this reduction was not significant in either case (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide, there was no evidence of a difference between short- and long-range correlation changes after clozapine administration.
source: We also found no evidence of a difference between short- and long-range correlation changes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing short- and long-range correlations.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, clozapine resulted in a significant reduction in both short- and long-range correlations.
source: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, however, we found a significant reduction in both short- and long-range correlations (Figure 6D and E), and both were more strongly reduced than in C57BL/6 mice that expressed GCaMP brain wide (C57BL/6 vs Tlx3-Cre × Ai148, short-range: p<0.05; long-range: p<10–5; rank-sum test).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: In mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, the reduction in activity correlations after clozapine was stronger for long-range correlations than it was for short-range correlations.
source: Moreover, the reduction in activity correlations was stronger for long-range correlations than it was for short-range correlations (Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Alterations in hemodynamic occlusion could not account for the decrease in correlations after clozapine but resulted in a small increase of the same metric.
source: To control for possible clozapine-induced changes in hemodynamic occlusion, we repeated the experiment and analyses in Tlx3-Cre mice that expressed eGFP in L5 IT neurons and found that alterations in hemodynamic occlusion could not account for the decrease in correlations but resulted in a small increase of the same metric (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: Saline injections resulted in no evidence of a change in correlations in Tlx3-Cre × Ai148 mice.
source: To test whether the stress of injection, or simply passage of time, could explain the observed effects, we conducted a separate set of experiments in which we injected saline in a cohort of Tlx3-Cre × Ai148 mice and performed the same analysis. We found no evidence of a change in correlations with saline injections (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F–H.

claim: While the activity correlations measured with widefield imaging decreased after clozapine in Tlx3-Cre × Ai148 mice, pairwise somatic activity correlations measured by two-photon imaging did not.
source: We found that while the activity correlations measured with the widefield imaging decreased (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C), pairwise somatic activity correlations measured by two-photon imaging did not (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: The finding that widefield correlations decreased while somatic correlations did not is consistent with the idea that decorrelation primarily occurs for long-range interactions.
source: This is consistent with the idea that decorrelation primarily occurs for long-range interactions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of widefield and two-photon imaging data.

claim: Clozapine decreased correlations of cortical activity in superficial excitatory neurons in Cux2-CreERT2 × Ai148 mice.
source: Finally, to confirm that the clozapine-induced reduction in correlation was stronger in deep cortical layers, we repeated the experiment in a population of L2/3 and L4 excitatory neurons using Cux2-CreERT2 × Ai148 mice. We found that clozapine also decreased correlations of cortical activity in superficial excitatory neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The reduction in correlations after clozapine in Cux2-CreERT2 × Ai148 mice was significantly weaker than the reduction observed in mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: However, this reduction was significantly weaker than the reduction we observed in mice that expressed GCaMP6 in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons (Cux2-CreERT2 × Ai148 vs Tlx3-Cre × Ai148, short-range: p<0.005, long-range: p<10–8, rank-sum test).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing the effects in different neuron types.

claim: Administration of the antipsychotic drug clozapine resulted in a decorrelation of activity across dorsal cortex that was stronger in L5 IT neurons (Tlx3) than it was in either upper layer excitatory neurons (Cux2) or in the brain wide average (C57BL/6).
source: Thus, administration of the antipsychotic drug clozapine resulted in a decorrelation of activity across dorsal cortex that was stronger in L5 IT neurons (Tlx3) than it was in either upper layer excitatory neurons (Cux2) or in the brain wide average (C57BL/6).
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the experimental data comparing different neuron types.

claim: The antipsychotic drug aripiprazole resulted in a decorrelation of the activity patterns of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: We found that the principal effect of decorrelation of the activity patterns of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons was preserved with both drugs (Figure 7A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A–F.

claim: The antipsychotic drug haloperidol resulted in a decorrelation of the activity patterns of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: We found that the principal effect of decorrelation of the activity patterns of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons was preserved with both drugs (Figure 7A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A–F.

claim: Changes in correlation after amphetamine injection were absent in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: These changes in correlation were absent upon injection of a psychostimulant, amphetamine (Figure 7G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G–I.

claim: A decrease in long-range correlations between cortical L5 IT neurons might be a common mechanism of action for antipsychotic drugs.
source: Thus, it is possible that a decrease in long-range correlations between cortical L5 IT neurons might be a common mechanism of action for antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a possibility based on the experimental data showing similar effects with multiple antipsychotic drugs.

claim: Changes in the correlation between cortical regions could either be driven by changes in correlated external inputs or through changes in communication between cortical regions.
source: Changes in the correlation between cortical regions could either be driven by changes in correlated external inputs or through changes in communication between cortical regions.
evidence: This is a statement about possible mechanisms underlying the observed changes in correlations.

claim: Mismatch responses were partially reduced in V1 and almost absent in V2am after injection of antipsychotic drugs in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: This is indeed what we observed: Mismatch responses were partially reduced in V1 and almost absent in V2am after injection of antipsychotic drugs (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Responses to onsets of drifting gratings were reduced in V2am after injection of antipsychotic drugs in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, but were overall less affected than mismatch responses.
source: While responses to onsets of drifting gratings were also reduced in V2am, they were overall less affected by the antipsychotic drugs than mismatch responses (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The results are consistent with the interpretation that antipsychotic drugs reduce lateral communication in L5.
source: These results are consistent with the interpretation that antipsychotic drugs reduce lateral communication in L5.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results showing reduced spread of prediction error responses.

claim: The source of the widefield imaging signal is likely a combination of somatic, dendritic, and axonal signals.
source: When interpreting our results, it should be kept in mind that the source of the widefield imaging signal in these experiments is not entirely clear and is likely a combination of somatic, dendritic, and axonal signals.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical limitations of the widefield imaging method.

claim: The signal attenuation half depth in cortex is on the order of 100 µm.
source: Given that the signal attenuation half depth in cortex is on the order of 100 µm (Aravanis et al., 2007), most signals likely come from the superficial 100 µm of tissue (Allen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aravanis et al., 2007 and Allen et al., 2017.

claim: Most widefield signals likely come from the superficial 100 µm of tissue.
source: Given that the signal attenuation half depth in cortex is on the order of 100 µm (Aravanis et al., 2007), most signals likely come from the superficial 100 µm of tissue (Allen et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Aravanis et al., 2007 and Allen et al., 2017.

claim: In the case of the Tlx3 recordings, the widefield signal is likely a mixture of axonal and dendritic signals of the Tlx3 neurons that have their soma in L5 but have a dense net of axons and dendrites in L1.
source: In the case of the Tlx3 recordings, this would mean that we were recording a mixture of axonal and dendritic signals of the Tlx3 neurons that have their soma in L5 but have a dense net of axons and dendrites in L1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomy of Tlx3 neurons and the properties of widefield imaging.

claim: In the case of the brain wide expression of GCaMP using an AAV-PHP.eB in C57BL/6 mice, the signals recorded likely also include contributions from thalamic axons.
source: In the case of the brain wide expression of GCaMP using an AAV-PHP.eB in C57BL/6 mice, the signals we recorded likely also include contributions from thalamic axons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of the AAV-PHP.eB and the anatomy of thalamocortical projections.

claim: There is a hemodynamic contribution to the widefield signal that is the result of varying occlusion by blood vessels.
source: In addition to this, there is a hemodynamic contribution to the signal (Allen et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2016; Valley et al., 2020) that is the result of varying occlusion by blood vessels.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Allen et al., 2017, Ma et al., 2016, and Valley et al., 2020.

claim: Accurate correction of hemodynamic responses likely requires calibration on eGFP measurements.
source: Accurate correction likely requires calibration on eGFP measurements (Valley et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Valley et al., 2020.

claim: Hemodynamic responses should not systematically differ between different mouse lines.
source: Given that hemodynamic responses should not systematically differ between different mouse lines, and that in the crystal skull preparation the contribution of hemodynamic occlusion to increases in fluorescence was relatively small (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), these hemodynamic artifacts should not substantially alter our conclusions.
evidence: This is a statement based on the assumption that hemodynamic responses are similar across mouse lines.

claim: In the crystal skull preparation, the contribution of hemodynamic occlusion to increases in fluorescence was relatively small.
source: Given that hemodynamic responses should not systematically differ between different mouse lines, and that in the crystal skull preparation the contribution of hemodynamic occlusion to increases in fluorescence was relatively small (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), these hemodynamic artifacts should not substantially alter our conclusions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Responses in widefield recordings inherently reflect population averages.
source: Lastly, it should be kept in mind that responses in these widefield recordings inherently reflect population averages.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of widefield imaging measurements.

claim: Assuming there is some form of lateral inhibition among neurons, population averages need not reflect responses of neurons that are tuned to the specific stimulus presented.
source: Assuming there is some form of lateral inhibition among neurons, population averages need not reflect responses of neurons that are tuned to the specific stimulus presented.
evidence: This is a statement about the interpretation of population averages in the presence of lateral inhibition.

claim: The suppression to grating stimuli observed in V1 Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons could be the result of a subset of Tlx3 neurons that are strongly responsive to the specific grating presented suppressing the rest of the population of Tlx3 neurons.
source: For example, the suppression to grating stimuli we observed in V1 Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons could be the result of a subset of Tlx3 neurons that are strongly responsive to the specific grating presented suppressing the rest of the population of Tlx3 neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed suppression in population responses.

claim: An understanding of the mechanism that results in opposing population responses of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons to positive and negative prediction errors will require measurements with single neuron resolution.
source: Thus, an understanding of the mechanism that results in opposing population responses of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons to positive and negative prediction errors will require measurements with single neuron resolution.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study and the need for future experiments.

claim: L5 IT neurons are densely connected to L5 pyramidal tract neurons.
source: In our experiments we have focused on Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, but given that L5 IT neurons are densely connected to L5 pyramidal tract neurons (Anderson et al., 2010; Kiritani et al., 2012) and to L6 neurons (Xu et al., 2016; Yamawaki and Shepherd, 2015), it is not unlikely that these neuron types would follow similar patterns of activity and exhibit similar susceptibility to the influence of antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2010 and Kiritani et al., 2012.

claim: L5 IT neurons are densely connected to L6 neurons.
source: In our experiments we have focused on Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, but given that L5 IT neurons are densely connected to L5 pyramidal tract neurons (Anderson et al., 2010; Kiritani et al., 2012) and to L6 neurons (Xu et al., 2016; Yamawaki and Shepherd, 2015), it is not unlikely that these neuron types would follow similar patterns of activity and exhibit similar susceptibility to the influence of antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2016 and Yamawaki and Shepherd, 2015.

claim: It is not unlikely that L5 pyramidal tract neurons and L6 neurons would follow similar patterns of activity and exhibit similar susceptibility to the influence of antipsychotic drugs as L5 IT neurons.
source: In our experiments we have focused on Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, but given that L5 IT neurons are densely connected to L5 pyramidal tract neurons (Anderson et al., 2010; Kiritani et al., 2012) and to L6 neurons (Xu et al., 2016; Yamawaki and Shepherd, 2015), it is not unlikely that these neuron types would follow similar patterns of activity and exhibit similar susceptibility to the influence of antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the anatomical connectivity between these neuron types.

claim: Ntsr1 positive L6 excitatory neurons exhibit similar levels of dissimilarity between closed and open loop locomotion onsets as those observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons.
source: In the comparison of closed and open loop locomotion onsets, we do indeed find that Ntsr1 positive L6 excitatory neurons exhibit similar levels of dissimilarity as those observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons (Figure 1L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Responses in the Ntsr1 recordings were noisier than those in the Tlx3 recordings, likely because of the lower dendritic and axonal volume of Ntsr1 positive neurons in L1.
source: It is possible that responses in the Ntsr1 recordings, however, were noisier than those in the Tlx3 recordings (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), likely because of the lower dendritic and axonal volume of Ntsr1 positive neurons in L1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical properties of Ntsr1 neurons and the observed data quality.

claim: It is possible that both the differential activation in closed and open loop locomotion onsets as well as the susceptibility of long-range correlations to antipsychotic drugs is a general feature of cortical L5 and L6.
source: Thus, while we have focused on the Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons mainly for reasons of experimental convenience, it is possible that both the differential activation in closed and open loop locomotion onsets as well as the susceptibility of long-range correlations to antipsychotic drugs is a general feature of cortical L5 and L6.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a possibility based on the experimental data.

claim: It is currently unclear whether the decorrelation effect observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons is specific to the Tlx3-Cre mouse line.
source: Another possibility we currently cannot entirely rule out is that the decorrelation effect we observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons is specific to the Tlx3-Cre mouse line.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the study.

claim: It seems unlikely that the decorrelation effect is specific to the Tlx3-Cre mouse line given that all mouse lines were maintained on the same C57BL/6 background.
source: However, this seems unlikely given that all mouse lines we used were maintained on the same C57BL/6 background.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental design and the genetic background of the mice.

claim: It is still unclear what the relevant sites of action in the brain are of antipsychotic drugs.
source: It is still unclear what the relevant sites of action in the brain are of antipsychotic drugs.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Antipsychotic drugs are often antagonists of the D2 receptors, which are most strongly expressed in striatum.
source: Antipsychotic drugs are often antagonists of the D2 receptors, which are most strongly expressed in striatum.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about antipsychotic drugs and D2 receptor expression.

claim: It is sometimes assumed that the relevant site of action of antipsychotics is the striatum.
source: Consequently, it is sometimes assumed that the relevant site of action of antipsychotics is the striatum.
evidence: This is a statement about a common assumption in the field.

claim: An increase in striatal dopamine activates auditory cortex.
source: Consistent with this, an increase in striatal dopamine activates auditory cortex (Maia and Frank, 2017) and mediates hallucination-like perceptions in mice (Schmack et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Maia and Frank, 2017.

claim: An increase in striatal dopamine mediates hallucination-like perceptions in mice.
source: Consistent with this, an increase in striatal dopamine activates auditory cortex (Maia and Frank, 2017) and mediates hallucination-like perceptions in mice (Schmack et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schmack et al., 2021.

claim: L5 IT neurons provide a dominant input to striatum.
source: It is intriguing, however, to speculate that the effects we observed in L5 IT neurons, which provide a dominant input to striatum (Morita et al., 2019), may be an alternate site of action.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Morita et al., 2019.

claim: It is unlikely that the primary site of action of the antipsychotic drugs with respect to the L5 decorrelation phenotype is striatum.
source: While it is possible that the primary site of action of the antipsychotic drugs with respect to the L5 decorrelation phenotype we observed is striatum, this is unlikely.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and anatomical considerations.

claim: Feedback from striatum to cortex is exclusively mediated through thalamus.
source: However, feedback from striatum to cortex is exclusively mediated through thalamus, and neither L4, the primary thalamo-recipient layer in cortex, nor our brain wide recordings exhibited any of the effects we saw in L5 IT neurons.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about striato-thalamo-cortical circuits.

claim: Neither L4 nor brain wide recordings exhibited any of the effects seen in L5 IT neurons after antipsychotic drug administration.
source: However, feedback from striatum to cortex is exclusively mediated through thalamus, and neither L4, the primary thalamo-recipient layer in cortex, nor our brain wide recordings exhibited any of the effects we saw in L5 IT neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data comparing different neuron types.

claim: Thalamocortical collaterals in deep layers come from thalamic neurons that project primarily to superficial layers.
source: Thalamocortical collaterals in deep layers, however, come from thalamic neurons that project primarily to superficial layers (Oberlaender et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oberlaender et al., 2012.

claim: It is unlikely that the observed effects in L5 IT neurons were inherited from striatum.
source: Thus, we think it is unlikely that the observed effects in L5 IT neurons were inherited from striatum.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and anatomical considerations.

claim: The long-range decorrelation of activity could be used as a basis for a functional screen for compounds with antipsychotic efficacy.
source: Independent of whether the treatment-relevant site of action of antipsychotic drugs is indeed in L5 IT neurons, or whether the observed decorrelation of activity is relevant to antipsychotic potency of these drugs, we speculate that the long-range decorrelation of activity could be used as a basis for a functional screen for compounds with antipsychotic efficacy.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: It might be possible to test for similar decorrelation effects in human subjects using layer-specific fMRI recordings.
source: Given that in the brain wide recordings the decorrelation of activity was weaker compared to that observed in Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons, it might be possible to test for similar effects in human subjects using layer-specific fMRI recordings (Haarsma et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential for translating the findings to human studies, supported by a citation to Haarsma et al., 2022.

claim: The dominant mode of coupling in cortex might be lateral, not vertical.
source: A rather surprising implication of our results is that the dominant mode of coupling in cortex might be lateral, not vertical.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: While L5 was differentially activated across cortical regions during closed and open loop locomotion onsets, L2/3 exhibited rather limited differences.
source: Two findings would argue for this interpretation. First, while L5 was differentially activated across cortical regions during closed and open loop locomotion onsets, L2/3 exhibited rather limited differences.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings comparing L5 and L2/3 responses.

claim: Antipsychotics decorrelated L5 activity but had no effect on L2/3.
source: Second, antipsychotics decorrelated L5 activity but had no effect on L2/3.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings comparing the effects of antipsychotics on L5 and L2/3.

claim: Both findings could be explained if the long-range lateral coupling within L5 is stronger than the local vertical coupling between L2/3 and L5.
source: Both findings could be explained if the long-range lateral coupling within L5 is stronger than the local vertical coupling between L2/3 and L5.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: It has been speculated that disrupted resting-state functional connectivity in brain networks involving cortex is central to the pathogenesis of schizophrenia.
source: It has been speculated that disrupted resting-state functional connectivity in brain networks involving cortex is central to the pathogenesis of schizophrenia (Li et al., 2017; Northoff and Duncan, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2017 and Northoff and Duncan, 2016.

claim: Treatment-naïve schizophrenia patients predominantly exhibit increases in resting-state functional connectivity between cortical regions.
source: Treatment-naïve schizophrenia patients predominantly exhibit increases in resting-state functional connectivity between cortical regions, while medicated schizophrenia patients exhibit more balanced fractions of increased and decreased functional connections (Anticevic et al., 2015; Du et al., 2021; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anticevic et al., 2015, Du et al., 2021, and Li et al., 2017.

claim: Medicated schizophrenia patients exhibit more balanced fractions of increased and decreased functional connections.
source: Treatment-naïve schizophrenia patients predominantly exhibit increases in resting-state functional connectivity between cortical regions, while medicated schizophrenia patients exhibit more balanced fractions of increased and decreased functional connections (Anticevic et al., 2015; Du et al., 2021; Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Anticevic et al., 2015, Du et al., 2021, and Li et al., 2017.

claim: Auditory hallucinations are associated with increased activation of diverse cortical regions.
source: Auditory hallucinations, one of the hallmark symptoms of schizophrenia, are associated with increased activation of diverse cortical regions (Catafau et al., 1994; Dierks et al., 1999; Shergill et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Catafau et al., 1994, Dierks et al., 1999, and Shergill et al., 2000.

claim: It is conceivable that antipsychotic drugs counteract increased cortical activation by reducing the strength of long-range cortical connectivity mediated by L5 IT neurons.
source: Thus, it is conceivable that antipsychotic drugs counteract this by reducing the strength of long-range cortical connectivity mediated by L5 IT neurons, independent of whether the increased activity in schizophrenic patients is indeed driven by aberrant increases in the strength of long-range cortical connections or is a consequence of an aberrant increase in the strength of striato-thalamo-cortical loops.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as conceivable, representing a speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: A direct involvement of cortical circuits in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia is consistent with the glutamate hypothesis of schizophrenia.
source: However, a direct involvement of cortical circuits in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia is consistent with the glutamate hypothesis of schizophrenia.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the experimental findings to an existing hypothesis in the field.

claim: The glutamate hypothesis of schizophrenia is based on the finding that NMDA receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms.
source: This hypothesis is based on the finding that NMDA receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms (Moghaddam and Javitt, 2012), and that disturbances of NMDA and AMPA receptor-related gene expression are associated with schizophrenia (Harrison and Weinberger, 2005; Singh et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Moghaddam and Javitt, 2012.

claim: Disturbances of NMDA and AMPA receptor-related gene expression are associated with schizophrenia.
source: This hypothesis is based on the finding that NMDA receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms (Moghaddam and Javitt, 2012), and that disturbances of NMDA and AMPA receptor-related gene expression are associated with schizophrenia (Harrison and Weinberger, 2005; Singh et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Harrison and Weinberger, 2005 and Singh et al., 2020.

claim: NMDA receptors are necessary during visual development to establish normal prediction error signaling in V1.
source: In V1, it has been shown that NMDA receptors are necessary during visual development to establish normal prediction error signaling (Widmer and Keller, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Widmer and Keller, 2021.

claim: It is conceivable that a disruption of glutamatergic signaling in cortex that alters the way internal representations are activated by prediction errors is central to the etiology of schizophrenia.
source: Thus, it is conceivable that a disruption of glutamatergic signaling in cortex that alters the way internal representations are activated by prediction errors is central to the etiology of schizophrenia.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as conceivable, representing a speculation based on the experimental findings and cited literature.

claim: If a disruption of glutamatergic signaling in cortex is central to the etiology of schizophrenia, we should find impairments in all domains of cortical function, including sensory processing.
source: If so, we should find impairments in all domains of cortical function, including sensory processing.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the speculation about glutamatergic signaling disruption.

claim: In the case of the sensory cortex, cortical dysfunctions should be apparent earlier in development, concurrent with the critical period for plasticity in sensory areas of cortex.
source: In the case of the sensory cortex, cortical dysfunctions should be apparent earlier in development, concurrent with the critical period for plasticity in sensory areas of cortex.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the speculation about cortical dysfunction in schizophrenia.

claim: The core symptoms of schizophrenia typically appear in late adolescence.
source: While the core symptoms of schizophrenia typically appear in late adolescence, sensory processing is indeed impaired in schizophrenic patients (Javitt, 2009) and is apparent, for example, in the reduction of surround suppression in V1 (Yoon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about the onset of schizophrenia symptoms.

claim: Sensory processing is impaired in schizophrenic patients.
source: While the core symptoms of schizophrenia typically appear in late adolescence, sensory processing is indeed impaired in schizophrenic patients (Javitt, 2009) and is apparent, for example, in the reduction of surround suppression in V1 (Yoon et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Javitt, 2009.

claim: Sensory processing impairments in schizophrenic patients are apparent in the reduction of surround suppression in V1.
source: While the core symptoms of schizophrenia typically appear in late adolescence, sensory processing is indeed impaired in schizophrenic patients (Javitt, 2009) and is apparent, for example, in the reduction of surround suppression in V1 (Yoon et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yoon et al., 2009.

claim: Some sensory disturbances are detectable already during childhood as visuo-perceptual and reading anomalies in some subjects that later develop schizophrenia.
source: Interestingly, some of these disturbances are detectable already during childhood as visuo-perceptual and reading anomalies in some subjects that later develop schizophrenia (Parellada et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Parellada et al., 2017.

claim: Positive symptoms of schizophrenia can be explained in a predictive processing framework of cortical function as a disturbance of a prediction error-based update of internal representations.
source: Positive symptoms of schizophrenia can be explained in a predictive processing framework of cortical function as a disturbance of a prediction error-based update of internal representations (Fletcher and Frith, 2009; Frith, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fletcher and Frith, 2009 and Frith, 2005.

claim: There are two types of prediction error neurons, positive and negative.
source: There are two types of prediction error neurons, positive and negative, and, given that cortex likely implements a non-hierarchical variant of predictive processing (Garner and Keller, 2022), two types of internal representation neurons.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about predictive processing.

claim: Cortex likely implements a non-hierarchical variant of predictive processing.
source: There are two types of prediction error neurons, positive and negative, and, given that cortex likely implements a non-hierarchical variant of predictive processing (Garner and Keller, 2022), two types of internal representation neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Garner and Keller, 2022.

claim: There are two types of internal representation neurons.
source: There are two types of prediction error neurons, positive and negative, and, given that cortex likely implements a non-hierarchical variant of predictive processing (Garner and Keller, 2022), two types of internal representation neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited work on non-hierarchical predictive processing.

claim: One set of internal representation neurons is excited by positive prediction errors and inhibited by negative prediction errors.
source: One set of internal representation neurons is excited by positive prediction errors and inhibited by negative prediction errors, and the other one is inhibited by positive prediction errors and excited by negative prediction errors (Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018.

claim: One set of internal representation neurons is inhibited by positive prediction errors and excited by negative prediction errors.
source: One set of internal representation neurons is excited by positive prediction errors and inhibited by negative prediction errors, and the other one is inhibited by positive prediction errors and excited by negative prediction errors (Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Keller and Mrsic-Flogel, 2018.

claim: Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons exhibited opposing responses to positive and negative prediction errors.
source: Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons exhibited opposing responses to positive and negative prediction errors (Figure 3), and, while several different interpretations are conceivable, these responses would be consistent with those of internal representation neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The responses of Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons to positive and negative prediction errors would be consistent with those of internal representation neurons.
source: Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons exhibited opposing responses to positive and negative prediction errors (Figure 3), and, while several different interpretations are conceivable, these responses would be consistent with those of internal representation neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and the theoretical framework of predictive processing.

claim: Anesthesia is thought to decouple L5 neuron soma from their apical tuft and thereby prevent conscious perception.
source: Given that the effects of antipsychotic drugs are predominantly observed in L5 IT neurons, and that anesthesia is thought to decouple L5 neuron soma from their apical tuft and thereby prevent conscious perception (Suzuki and Larkum, 2020), we speculate that Tlx3 positive L5 IT neurons may be one type of internal representation neuron and one of the functionally relevant sites of antipsychotic action.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Suzuki and Larkum, 2020.
